controls.name: Agent ID
controls.definition: Stable agent and workload identity linked to an owner, runtime and release.

controls.name: Credential Brokerage
controls.definition: Scoped credential delivery, rotation, expiry and revocation without exposing secrets to model context.

controls.name: Delegation (OBO)
controls.definition: Propagation of the initiating user identity and delegated authority to downstream services.

controls.name: A2A
controls.definition: Authenticated and authorised communication between agents across defined trust boundaries.

controls.name: Agent Local Scopes
controls.definition: Permissable actions in local host environment

controls.name: Agent Remote Scopes
controls.definition: Permissable actions against connected systems

controls.name: Human Approval
controls.definition: An authorised human decision bound to the exact proposed action, with denial and replay handling.

controls.name: Agent Provisioning
controls.definition: Controlled creation, change and retirement of agent identities, permissions and configurations.

controls.name: Agent Orchestration
controls.definition: Workflow sequencing, delegation, cancellation, retry and recovery.

controls.name: Inference
controls.definition: Model execution with explicit version, endpoint, data handling and operating limits.

controls.name: Execution Environment
controls.definition: The local host of harness, code interpreter, networking

controls.name: Agent In-Session Memory
controls.definition: Session-scoped state with access control, resumption and retention.

controls.name: Harness
controls.definition: The software harness executing tools

controls.name: Agent Persistent Memory
controls.definition: Cross-session, long-term chat/session history

controls.name: Model Gateway
controls.definition: enforce per agent/user/workload routing, quota/cost & rates, injection screening?

controls.name: Tool Gateway
controls.definition: enforce per agent/user/workload allowed tools, schemas, auth config, quota & rates, dangerous action filtering, injection screening? Inc internet egress

controls.name: Data Gateway
controls.definition: enforce per agent/user/workload retrieval, DLP

controls.name: A2A Gateway
controls.definition: enforce per agent/user/workload allowed A2A pairs, schemas

controls.name: HITL
controls.definition: Human Review of Output

controls.name: Behavioural
controls.definition: Task training, continuous validation, anomaly detection

controls.name: Cost & Yield
controls.definition: Token, infrastructure, labour costs & savings, output increase, profit

controls.name: Infrastructure
controls.definition: Load Performance, Anomaly Detection

controls.name: Connectivity
controls.definition: Human readable view of agent network reach & potential action scopes against downstream systems

controls.name: Administrative Audit
controls.definition: Tamper-proof ledger of actions by user/agent/session, input, output, reasoning

controls.name: SOC Telemetry
controls.definition: Security telemetry with session and actor correlation, redaction, detections and response ownership.

controls.name: Model Assurance
controls.definition: Model file inspection, model lineage & compliance attestation, AI BoM

controls.name: Runtime Assurance
controls.definition: Inference & tool execution containers, harness, hosts

controls.name: First-Party Tool Assurance
controls.definition: SBOM, scanning, review, defence of firsty and third party MCP servers, CLIs,skills, extensions, external third party services, egress.

controls.name: Third-Party Tool Assurance
controls.definition: Where third party MCP registries, CLI, skills, plugins used - scanning for squatting, tool meta poisoning, package/plugin compromise.

controls.name: Data & Feature Stores
controls.definition: Governance, sanitisation, infra

controls.name: AI Discovery
controls.definition: Shadow AI

controls.name: Automated AI Pen-Testing
controls.definition: Authorised automated adversarial testing of model, retrieval, tool and runtime boundaries.

controls.name: Asset Registries & Inventory
controls.definition: Inventory and registration of models, agents and tools, including schemas and software component records. The inherited AWS finding covers the former combined policy and inventory scope.

controls.name: Registration & Approval Workflows
controls.definition: Submission, registration and approval of models, agents and tools. Research ongoing changes separately under Change & Release Governance. The inherited AWS finding retains its original broader scope.

controls.name: Posture & Reporting
controls.definition: Visibility into control coverage, policy breaches, unresolved risks and governance status.

controls.name: Policy Management
controls.definition: Definition, ownership, versioning, publication and review of AI policies. Research enforcement mechanisms under the gateway capabilities.

controls.name: AI Lifecycle Management
controls.definition: How models, agents and use cases move from proposal through testing, production, change and retirement.

controls.name: Ownership & Accountability
controls.definition: Assignment and maintenance of accountable owners for agents, models, tools and their decisions.

controls.name: Risk Assessment & Classification
controls.definition: Assessment of use cases, assignment of risk levels and selection of appropriate controls.

controls.name: Change & Release Governance
controls.definition: Approval, versioning, release and rollback of changes to models, prompts, tools, permissions and knowledge.

controls.name: Exceptions & Risk Acceptance
controls.definition: Recording, approval, expiry and review of policy exceptions and accepted risks.

controls.name: Data Lifecycle Governance
controls.definition: Governance of retention, deletion, residency and permitted use across inputs, outputs and agent memory.

controls.name: Assurance & Compliance Evidence
controls.definition: Collection and traceability of control evidence against requirements, assessments and audits.

controls.name: Third-Party Governance
controls.definition: Approval, periodic reassessment and retirement of external models, tools and services. Research technical scanning separately under tool assurance.

records.answer: Agent Identity gives each agent deployed to Agent Runtime a SPIFFE-based IAM principal derived from its reasoningEngines resource ID, with an auto-provisioned X.509 certificate valid for 24 hours. Grants use the principal:// identifier and principalSet bindings can cover all agents in a project or organisation. Without the identity flag, Agent Runtime falls back to service accounts.
records.gaps: No documented owner attribute. Redeploying an agent creates a new principal and existing grants do not carry over. The identity is tied to the resource, not to a revision or release. Manage agent access still labels agent identity preview.
records.options: Record owner and release in Agent Registry entries or resource labels. Use project-scoped principalSet bindings for baseline grants and check grants after each redeploy.

records.answer: The Agent Identity auth manager is a credential vault and broker for API keys, OAuth client credentials and delegated end-user tokens, governed by IAM. Agent X.509 certificates renew every 24 hours and Google Cloud access tokens are bound to them, with mTLS and DPoP through Agent Gateway. In the Gemini Enterprise connector path, credentials are decrypted at the gateway so the agent never sees the raw credential.
records.gaps: With ADK on Agent Runtime the token is injected into tool invocation headers inside agent code, and the docs do not state it stays out of model context. Revocation of consent and tokens is not described on the pages read. The 3-legged OAuth page is preview.
records.options: Route tool calls through Agent Gateway so credentials are attached at the gateway. Test that tokens never appear in traces, sessions or prompts.

records.answer: Agents can act with user-delegated authority through a 3-legged OAuth auth provider: the user signs in and consents, the auth manager stores the tokens in a Google-managed vault, and the agent retrieves them for tool calls. End-user access events are attributable to the agent's SPIFFE ID. Agent Runtime also supports an OAuth client ID per agent for end-user consent.
records.gaps: Feature is preview and the IAM Connectors API will not reach GA. No documented propagation of the initiating user identity to Google Cloud APIs or to downstream agents in a chain. Revocation not described.
records.options: Use the Agent Identity API path for new projects. Test whether downstream audit logs record both the user and the agent identity.

records.gaps: A2A on Agent Runtime is preview. Share an agent warns that Agent Runtime provides only coarse access control and A2A agents need their own authentication for untrusted callers. Trust boundaries across organisations are not described.

records.answer: Agent evaluation runs test sets with graders for general quality, content safety, compare meaning, tool use, keyword, text similarity, exact match and custom criteria. Security analytics show trends of blocked messages, and Defender raises near-real-time alerts on jailbreak, XPIA and other agent behaviour.
records.gaps: Evaluation is run on demand, and continuous scheduled validation is not described. Behavioural anomaly detection depends on Defender, which is preview for agents.
records.options: Run evaluation test sets in the ALM pipeline before each release and enable Defender security for AI.

records.answer: The Power Platform admin center shows Copilot Credit consumption by environment, agent and user with downloadable reports that include channel, model and tool. Admins set monthly per-agent limits. The Copilot Studio Monitor page has a savings calculator for time and cost saved per run or per tool.
records.gaps: Savings figures come from maker estimates, not measured baselines. Admins can turn off cost savings.
records.options: Record baseline task times before deployment and compare with consumption reports.

records.answer: Agents can send telemetry to Azure Application Insights, and a Copilot Studio dashboard workbook (preview) shows conversations, latency, exceptions and tool usage. Environment-level telemetry is also available in preview.
records.gaps: Telemetry is opt-in per agent and needs a customer Azure resource. Anomaly detection is not built in.
records.options: Connect Application Insights and add Azure Monitor alerts on latency and exceptions.

records.answer: Entra admins can see the connectors an agent may call as API permissions on its Agent ID without opening the Power Platform admin center. The inventory lists each connector operation, whether it is a tool or knowledge, when it can be used, and whether the connection is the user's or the maker's.
records.gaps: Custom connectors, MCP servers and REST API tools add no Entra scopes. Inventory capability fields are preview and capped at 200 resources per type.
records.options: Use inventory exports through Azure Resource Graph to build a connector reach view per agent.

records.answer: Purview logs maker and admin events such as BotCreate, BotPublish, BotShare and component changes, plus CopilotInteraction events for user use with a transcript thread ID. Collection cannot be disabled, and DSPM for AI retrieves the chat text. Entra logs agent identity sign-ins.
records.gaps: Audit records do not hold the transcript or reasoning. Some channels are excluded. FedRAMP tenants are excluded. Tamper evidence is not stated. Audit can be disabled in Purview tenant-wide.
records.options: Export audit and transcripts to immutable storage and test channel coverage.

records.answer: Admins can monitor and alert on agent activities through Microsoft Sentinel. Microsoft Defender correlates agent alerts into incidents and exposes Advanced Hunting tables for agent inventory, activity and real-time protection behaviours, with redacted prompt evidence.
records.gaps: Defender detection is preview and a separate product. Prompt Shields block events are not yet recorded as behaviours for Copilot Studio agents.
records.options: Connect Copilot Studio to Defender and route alerts to the SOC with named owners.

records.answer: Copilot Studio tags models as GA, preview, experimental, retired or cross-geo and notes Microsoft's own safety evaluation of one experimental model. No model file inspection, lineage record, attestation or AI bill of materials is documented.
records.gaps: Customers cannot inspect or attest the hosted models.
records.options: Request model cards and responsible AI documentation from Microsoft and model providers.

records.answer: Copilot Studio follows Microsoft's Security Development Lifecycle, and the GitHub Copilot harness runs tasks in a sandbox. Cloud PC pools for computer use are Entra joined and Intune enrolled, and Microsoft gives hardening advice for customer machines.
records.gaps: No customer-visible assurance of inference or tool execution containers. Customer machines are the customer's responsibility.
records.options: Use Service Trust Portal reports for platform assurance and manage computer use machines under endpoint controls.

records.answer: An automatic security scan warns makers before publishing when an agent has no authentication, uses maker-provided credentials or is shared organisation-wide. Real-time risk assessment flags exfiltration risks while configuring knowledge, tools and actions. MCP connectors can go through connector certification to be used across tenants.
records.gaps: No SBOM, code scanning or review of MCP servers, connectors or skills is documented. Scan findings are warnings.
records.options: Review custom connectors and MCP servers in an internal process before adding them to business data groups.

records.answer: Copilot Studio reflects MCP server tool changes automatically and states the customer is responsible for tools from external MCP servers. Checked the MCP and data policy pages: admins can block connectors, but there is no scanning for squatting, tool metadata poisoning or package compromise.
records.gaps: Dynamic MCP tool updates mean a changed tool description is used without review.
records.options: Pin MCP servers to vetted endpoints and use external threat detection to screen tool calls at runtime.

records.answer: Knowledge sources are governed by data policies that block uploads, SharePoint, OneDrive or public websites, with endpoint filtering. Agent data lives in Dataverse environments that support customer-managed keys and sensitivity labels show on SharePoint-grounded answers.
records.gaps: No sanitisation or poisoning checks on knowledge content are documented.
records.options: Limit knowledge to curated SharePoint sites through endpoint filtering and label sources.

records.answer: The agent inventory gives admins a tenant view of all Copilot Studio and Agent Builder agents, including drafts, with creator, owner, channels, authentication and connectors. This surfaces maker-built agents that IT did not commission.
records.gaps: Covers only agents built in Copilot Studio and Agent Builder, not other AI tools. Classic V1 agents are excluded. The inventory is preview.
records.options: Pair the inventory with Agent 365 or Defender for wider AI discovery.

records.answer: Agent evaluation tests quality, tool use and content safety of responses but does not generate adversarial attacks. Checked the evaluation, security and threat detection pages and found no automated red-teaming of model, retrieval, tool or runtime boundaries.
records.gaps: Prompt injection resistance must be tested with external tools.
records.options: Use an external red-teaming tool against published agents in a test environment.

records.answer: The agent inventory records each agent's harness, IDs, creator, owner, environment, publish date, Entra identity, model, authentication, channels, sharing and connector operations. Data is available in the Power Platform admin center, the Power Platform API and Azure Resource Graph and refreshes within about 20 minutes.
records.gaps: The page is preview and many configuration fields are preview. Only connectors and web search are detailed among capabilities. Classic bots are excluded.
records.options: Query Azure Resource Graph on a schedule and reconcile with Entra Agent IDs.

records.answer: Admins control who can author agents, which features makers may use through data policies, and whether agents using generative AI can be published. Microsoft 365 admins govern which agents appear in Microsoft Copilot, and org-wide sharing can require admin approval.
records.gaps: No built-in submission and approval workflow for new agents or tools is documented in Copilot Studio.
records.options: Use Power Platform pipelines and solution deployment as the approval gate into production environments.

records.answer: Each published agent shows a protection status of Protected, Needs review or Unknown across authentication, policies and content moderation, with blocked-message analytics. Data policy violations are listed per agent and admins can see inventory and credit status across the tenant.
records.gaps: Protection status is a maker view per agent. No tenant-wide control coverage report is documented in Copilot Studio.
records.options: Build a posture report from inventory, audit and Defender data.

records.answer: Data policies are defined by tenant or environment admins in the Power Platform admin center, scoped to all, selected or excluded environments, with custom admin contact and learn-more links on violations. A maker welcome message can state privacy and compliance requirements.
records.gaps: Policy versioning, ownership records and review cycles are not documented.
records.options: Keep policy definitions in source control and review them on a schedule.

records.answer: Microsoft's ALM guidance uses development, test and production environments, solutions, environment variables, Git integration and pipelines, Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions to move agents. Agents can be quarantined and deleted, and retired models remain usable for one month.
records.gaps: Authentication, channels and sharing are not solution-aware and need post-deployment steps. Multistage approvals lack ALM support.
records.options: Script post-deployment configuration for non-solution-aware settings.

records.answer: Copilot Studio adds the agent owner as a sponsor on the Entra Agent ID for traceability and accountability. The inventory records createdBy and the current ownerId, and the creator of each connector operation.
records.gaps: Some preexisting agents have no sponsor. Reassignment when an owner leaves is not described in Copilot Studio docs.
records.options: Use Entra ID Governance to review sponsors and reassign orphaned agents.

records.answer: Copilot Studio flags technical risks through the pre-publish security scan and real-time risk findings. Checked the security and governance pages and found no use-case risk assessment or risk-tier classification that selects controls.
records.gaps: Risk classification must be run outside the product.
records.options: Record risk tiers in an external register and map tiers to environments and data policies.

records.answer: Changes take effect only when an agent is published, and publish, update and component changes are audited. Agents move between environments as managed solutions through pipelines or Git with deployment history, and version control supports rollback.
records.gaps: Rollback relies on redeploying an earlier solution version. Model changes through the default upgrade are not release-gated.
records.options: Pin a GA model and deploy only managed solutions through approved pipelines.

records.answer: Copilot Studio removed agent data policy enforcement exemptions. Checked the data policy and governance pages and found no feature to record, approve or expire policy exceptions.
records.gaps: Exceptions are handled by changing policy scope, with no expiry or record.
records.options: Track exceptions in an external register and use a separate environment with its own data policy.

records.answer: Data stays in the environment's chosen geography, with EU Data Boundary support and an admin setting for cross-region data movement. Transcripts are deleted after 30 days in Dataverse by default and 28 days in Copilot Studio storage, memory after 28 days of inactivity, and Purview retention policies can retain user and agent text for zero days. Customer-managed keys are supported.
records.gaps: Cross-geo and external models can process data outside the region. External threat detection providers may store data elsewhere.
records.options: Disable cross-region data movement and external models where residency is required.

records.answer: Copilot Studio lists SOC, ISO 27001 and related ISO standards, HIPAA BAA coverage, PCI DSS, CSA STAR and others, with audit reports in the Microsoft Service Trust Portal. Purview audit logs and DSPM for AI provide customer-side activity evidence.
records.gaps: No mapping of agent controls to customer requirements or assessments is provided.
records.options: Map Purview and inventory evidence to the organisation's control framework.

records.answer: Admins must turn on external models per environment and allow each provider, such as Anthropic, Mistral or xAI, in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Microsoft states makers are responsible for external A2A agents and MCP servers, and connectors can be blocked by data policy.
records.gaps: No periodic reassessment or retirement workflow for external models, tools or services.
records.options: Review allowed providers and connectors on a fixed cycle and record decisions externally.

records.answer: AI agents can run as a dedicated AI user, a User [sys_user] record with the AI user identity type and its own fixed roles (Zurich and Brazil). AI Control Tower registers agents as AI assets with lifecycle, risk and owner roles, and Build Agent registers generated agents there (Brazil). The default identity is the dynamic invoking user, so most agents have no distinct workload identity.
records.gaps: AI user is optional. No documented binding of an agent identity to a specific runtime or release version.
records.options: Require an AI user per production agent and record it on the AI Control Tower asset. Test that execution records show the AI user.

records.answer: Cowork can log in to websites with stored credential parameters, and the page says sensitive values are kept out of the chat and the agent's plan (Brazil). A2A and MCP connections use Connection and Credential Alias records, and MCP OAuth 2.1 records hold a token revocation URL (Brazil). Rotation, expiry and storage protection of these credentials are not described on the pages read.
records.gaps: No documented rotation or expiry. The Cowork page does not say whether the model receives credential values.
records.options: Use OAuth with short-lived tokens where possible and review platform credential store documentation. Test that secrets never appear in execution plans or traces.

records.answer: By default an agent runs as the dynamic user, meaning the invoking user or the calling workflow's user, and tools always run as dynamic users (Zurich and Brazil). Role masking limits the agent to the intersection of the invoker's roles and an approved list and never adds roles (Brazil). Propagation of the user's identity to external MCP or A2A services is not documented, and inbound A2A uses a service account.
records.gaps: OBO to external systems unclear. MCP OAuth Client Credentials grant uses an administrator token. Inbound A2A runs as a configured service account.
records.options: Use OAuth Authorization Code grants for MCP servers and confirm per-user tokens in testing. Map inbound A2A callers to narrow service accounts.

records.answer: AI Agent Studio supports the Agent2Agent protocol for external agents and exposes ServiceNow agents as secondary agents through an Agent Card endpoint (Brazil). Inbound calls authenticate with OAuth 2.0 or an API key tied to a service account and an A2A auth scope, attached to the AI Agent A2A API Access Policy. Outbound calls use Connection and Credential Alias records, and ACLs apply to external AI agents.
records.gaps: Exposure is enabled by an instance-wide toggle with no documented per-agent filter. Per-caller authorisation beyond service account roles is not described. The two auth scope names on the setup page disagree.
records.options: Create one service account and OAuth client per partner platform with minimal roles. Test that unexposed agents reject calls.

records.answer: Cowork runs actions inside an isolated virtual environment with file system boundaries, protected credential paths, file type read, write or deny rules and a network allow list, set by administrators per user or group (Brazil). On the instance, ACLs, run-as identity and role masking bound what an agent can do, and Build Agent scripts run only in the target app scope (Brazil).
records.gaps: Shell controls are not covered on the Cowork page. Local MCP servers run outside the sandbox.
records.options: Turn off local MCP servers by policy and test sandbox deny rules.

records.answer: Agents act on connected systems through tools the builder adds, with each tool's run-as identity and role masking applied (Brazil). MCP tools can be set to allow, block or supervised in the Assistant, MCP Server Console limits exposed tools and fields, and Cowork connector scopes limit actions on a service regardless of the credential (Brazil).
records.gaps: The MCP server ACL does not apply when an AI agent uses the server. Scope on external systems otherwise depends on the connection credential.
records.options: Use least-privilege credentials per MCP connection and review tool lists per agent.

records.answer: Each tool can be set to Supervised so the agent pauses for human approval before it runs, and unattended runs stall until someone responds (Brazil). Cowork holds actions for approval, hard gate actions always need a human decision, and TOTP can be required for sensitive action approvals (Brazil). Build Agent shows the script, intent and target scope before each background script run.
records.gaps: Binding of approval to the exact parameters and replay handling are not documented. Cowork Allow always covers later actions of the same type.
records.options: Use hard gates for destructive Cowork actions and test that a changed action re-prompts.

records.answer: AI Control Tower can require AI steward approval before AI skills, agents and models deploy, and can block unapproved MCP servers in AI Agent Studio, though these controls are off by default (Brazil). AI users are created as User records, ACLs and role masks are set in guided setup, and new instances from the Australia release deny agents lacking explicit ACLs. Agents can be deactivated, and AI Control Tower flags...
records.gaps: Steward approval and deny by default must be turned on for upgraded instances.
records.options: Activate steward approval and the deny by default option and confirm with a test deployment.

records.answer: Agentic workflows coordinate one or more AI agents to move a process from start to finish, with triggers to start runs (Brazil). Cowork has turn caps, check-in pauses and a retry limit that stops and reports instead of retrying indefinitely (Brazil).
records.gaps: Cancellation, retry and recovery behaviour for AI Agent Studio runs was not found in the pages read.
records.options: Test failure, timeout and cancel behaviour of agentic workflows in a sub-production instance.

records.answer: Administrators choose the provider for agentic AI (Now LLM Service, AWS Claude, Azure OpenAI or Google Gemini) and can set target model versions per instance or skill (Brazil). Zurich settings cover regional or global data routing and an overflow option that keeps traffic in ServiceNow datacentres, and Generative AI Controller sets hourly request limits per provider, capability, instance or user.
records.gaps: Model choice for agents is global, not per agent. Web search grounding with Google is not data resident.
records.options: Pin target versions and test agents after provider changes as the page advises.

records.answer: Cowork runs actions in an isolated virtual environment with file system and network egress rules (Brazil). AI Agent Studio agents and script tools run on the ServiceNow instance, and the script tool page does not describe a sandbox or run-as identity.
records.gaps: No documented isolation for agent script tools on the instance.
records.options: Mark script tools Supervised and review them under the same controls as other server-side scripts.

records.answer: The pages read describe execution plans, sessions and long-term memory but not session-scoped state, its access control, resumption or retention for AI agents.
records.gaps: Short-term memory handling is not documented in the pages read.
records.options: Request ServiceNow documentation on execution plan and conversation state retention.

records.answer: The AI Agent Studio runtime executes agent tools, including skills, flow actions, subflows, scripts, record operations, search retrieval, web search, desktop actions and MCP tools, with per-tool execution modes (Brazil). The Cowork client enforces policy in its own code and checks every action against the active policy before it runs.
records.gaps: Internal harness design is not documented.
records.options: Treat the harness as vendor-operated and test policy enforcement with blocked actions.

records.answer: Long-term memory stores user facts and preferences, and optionally learning from past executions, as semantic memories scoped by user and category in the AI Agent Memories table (Brazil). Administrators toggle retention and map categories to agents individually.
records.gaps: Retention period, deletion and end-user controls are not described. No sensitive data exclusion rules are documented.
records.options: Limit categories per agent and test deletion of user memories before enabling.

records.answer: Generative AI Controller rate limit rules count requests per hour per provider, capability or all capabilities, either instance-wide or per user (Brazil). AI Guardian prompt injection detection covers all generative AI features on the instance in log or block mode, and custom guardians can call an external model.
records.gaps: No per-agent routing or cost quota. Prompt injection detection may miss attempts, per the page.
records.options: Set per-user rate rules and run Guardian in log mode before blocking.

records.answer: AI Gateway mediates MCP traffic with global and per-server pause, OAuth 2.1 client registration, a data sensitivity policy, and tool scanning against OWASP MCP Top 10 categories with auto-deactivation of vulnerable tools (Brazil). Cowork blocks outbound traffic except to an allow list, and MCP tools can be allowed, blocked or supervised.
records.gaps: Gateway covers MCP only. MCP rate limits are not configurable. Per-agent tool policy and logging are not described.
records.options: Route all agent MCP traffic through AI Gateway and test pause and tool deactivation.

records.answer: The AI Gateway Data Sensitivity Check scans MCP tool inputs and outputs and can block or flag sensitive content (Brazil). Now Assist privacy policies de-identify PII, and skills using AI Guardian remove PII before the request reaches the model. Retrieval is bounded by the agent's run-as identity and role masking.
records.gaps: Per-agent DLP policy is not described. Privacy policy scope is not listed.
records.options: Configure sensitive data types and test blocking on a tool with seeded test PII.

records.answer: The AI Gateway page describes MCP mediation only. A2A setup attaches authentication profiles to an access policy, but no gateway enforcing allowed agent pairs or schemas is documented.
records.gaps: No A2A pair allow lists or schema enforcement.
records.options: Use an external API gateway in front of the A2A endpoints.

records.answer: Supervised tools pause for a person before execution (Brazil). The activity view records thumbs up or down feedback with a required reason for negative ratings, and Cowork can pause at a set turn to ask whether to continue.
records.gaps: No documented review queue for agent outputs before release to users.
records.options: Use Supervised tools for customer-facing writes and sample outputs through AI Control Tower monitoring.

records.answer: AI Control Tower scores a sample of live interactions against configurable quality and safety metrics so stewards can find regressions, covering ServiceNow and external systems (Brazil). AI Agent Studio evaluations run test scenarios with task completion and other metrics, and Cowork traces are scored too.
records.gaps: Anomaly detection is not described. Evaluations are launched manually and custom metrics are not supported from AI Agent Studio.
records.options: Schedule evaluations after each instruction version change.

records.answer: AI Control Tower Measure converts usage into a productivity figure, records AI costs including token-level costs across providers, and reports net AI return by user and department (Brazil). The AI Agent Analytics dashboard counts assists per agent and workflow.
records.gaps: Productivity values depend on rates and vendor prices entered by the customer.
records.options: Reconcile Measure cost figures against provider invoices.

records.answer: The AI Agent Analytics dashboard shows P90, P95 and P99 latency for workflows, agents, tools and LLM requests, errors per hour and blocked executions (Brazil). Email notifications cover assist usage spikes, failed executions and latency errors.
records.gaps: Notification thresholds and anomaly logic are not defined on the page.
records.options: Set notification recipients per alert record and test with a forced failure.

records.answer: The AI Control Tower access map is a node graph of ServiceNow agents, agentic workflows and tools that flags access issues, and the security dashboard charts authorised and failed MCP client to server attempts (Brazil).
records.gaps: Covers ServiceNow agents. Downstream action scopes in external systems are not shown.
records.options: Combine the access map with connection credential scopes for external systems.

records.answer: Execution plans record agent runs, with the external prompt held in the Objective field for A2A runs (Brazil). The activity view gives task execution history and states, version logs filter activity by instruction version, Guardian logs record request details, and Cowork sends run and tool call spans to the instance.
records.gaps: Tamper resistance, reasoning capture and retention are not documented.
records.options: Confirm which tables are audited and export records to an immutable store.

records.answer: The AI Control Tower security dashboard reports prompt injection, sensitive data, agent goal hijacking and PII in output, and creates security tasks assigned to asset owners (Brazil). Guardian logs classify events into 16 safety categories and export as CSV.
records.gaps: No documented SIEM forwarding or log retention. Some metrics are missing on domain-separated instances.
records.options: Export Guardian and execution records to the SOC on a schedule and test correlation by user.

records.answer: AI Control Tower inventories models and can require steward approval before a model is deployed (Brazil). Model versions marked deprecated, retired, in review or rejected cannot be selected, and assets can be classified against NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act.
records.gaps: No model file inspection, lineage or AI bill of materials documented.
records.options: Request provider model documentation and record it on the asset.

records.answer: Cowork actions run in an isolated virtual environment with default protections that cannot be removed (Brazil). Build Agent scripts fail rather than fall back to global scope when the target cannot be resolved. Assurance of the instance hosts running inference and tools is not described in the pages read.
records.gaps: No runtime attestation or host assurance evidence in product docs.
records.options: Use ServiceNow compliance reports for hosting assurance.

records.answer: AI Gateway scans MCP tools against OWASP MCP Top 10 threat categories before activation, with optional Guardian and advanced scanning, and can auto-deactivate vulnerable tools (Brazil). AI ACLs are required before a subflow or action is exposed as an MCP tool.
records.gaps: No SBOM or code review process for first-party tools documented. Toggle descriptions do not match labels.
records.options: Confirm scanning results for each server and test with a deliberately poisoned description.

records.answer: Stewards can block unapproved MCP servers in AI Agent Studio, and registered servers pass through an approval playbook and AI Gateway tool scanning (Brazil). Cowork administrators can turn off local MCP servers, which run outside the sandbox.
records.gaps: No documented checks for registry squatting or package compromise. Local MCP has no allow list, only off.
records.options: Turn on MCP approval and test that an unapproved server shows the approval error.

records.answer: The AI Control Tower inventory records datasets alongside systems and models, and dataset change requests go through steward review (Brazil).
records.gaps: Sanitisation and storage infrastructure for agent knowledge sources are not described in the pages read.
records.options: Register knowledge sources as datasets and apply Now Assist privacy policies.

records.answer: AI Control Tower syncs AI assets from external platforms including AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, hyperscaler traces and Service Graph Connectors into one inventory, and discovered assets enter as unmanaged (Brazil).
records.gaps: No documented discovery of unsanctioned SaaS or endpoint AI use.
records.options: Pair with network or CASB discovery for user-side shadow AI.

records.answer: Checked evaluation, Guardian and AI Gateway pages. Evaluations run saved test scenarios for task completion, and no automated adversarial testing of models, retrieval or tools is documented.
records.gaps: No automated red teaming.
records.options: Use an external AI red teaming tool against a sub-production instance.

records.answer: AI Control Tower keeps a central inventory of AI systems, models, prompts, datasets and MCP servers from ServiceNow and external platforms, and Build Agent agents are registered there (Brazil). MCP server records show state, approval status and risk classification.
records.gaps: Tool-level schemas and software component records are not described.
records.options: Use the AI Inventory Intelligence Agent to find incomplete records.

records.answer: AI steward approval can gate deployment of AI systems, models and MCP servers, and playbooks create approval requests automatically when active (Brazil). AI intake request forms submit systems, models and datasets for evaluation, and stewards mark agents publishable.
records.gaps: Approvals are off by default. The configuration and approvals pages disagree on who can start manual requests.
records.options: Activate approvals and playbooks and confirm the manual role on the instance.

records.answer: AI Control Tower shows an AI asset security score, privileged and dormant agent charts and policy violations, plus compliance scores and a risk heat map (Brazil).
records.gaps: Security dashboard gaps on domain-separated instances.
records.options: Review weights and muted assets in the security score.

records.answer: Compliance is measured against authority documents and organisational policies through AI Risk and Compliance (Brazil). Cowork policies are authored centrally, merged by priority with a non-editable Default Policy and pushed to clients.
records.gaps: Policy versioning, ownership and review cycles are not described in the pages read.
records.options: Use GRC policy records for ownership and review dates.

records.answer: Playbooks move assets through onboarding, assessment, build and test, and deployment, with state values from Ideation to Deployed (Brazil). The Plan area tracks AI demand and priorities, and assets can be moved to unmanaged when pending retirement.
records.gaps: Use case intake detail and formal retirement steps are thin. Plan needs an SPM Professional licence.
records.options: Map lifecycle states to the organisation's stage gates.

records.answer: AI asset owners manage owned assets and approvals, and AI stewards oversee the portfolio (Brazil). Security tasks such as dormant agent reviews are assigned to owners.
records.gaps: Owner field on MCP server records is not described.
records.options: Make owner a required field and test task routing.

records.answer: Risk assessments rate assets high, medium, low or unacceptable, an initial rating is set from the Use and purpose field, and assets are classified against NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act (Brazil).
records.gaps: Control selection logic per risk level is not described.
records.options: Configure assessment templates and test with a sample high risk use case.

records.answer: Asset owners submit change requests that stewards approve, generating change tasks and a new asset record in onboarding (Brazil). Agent instructions have named versions with revert by switching the active version, model target versions are set per instance or skill, and Build Agent offers approved rollback of its scripts.
records.gaps: Instruction version activation has no documented approval step. Tool and permission changes are not versioned on the pages read.
records.options: Require change requests before activating new instruction versions.

records.answer: Policy exceptions are tracked per asset and in portfolio views, and appear as governance work in Activity Center (Brazil).
records.gaps: Approval, expiry and review of exceptions are not described in the pages read.
records.options: Use GRC policy exception workflows with expiry dates.

records.answer: Data sharing with ServiceNow is on by default and can be opted out, overflow processing to Azure can be turned off, and Zurich adds regional or global routing (Brazil and Zurich). Now Assist privacy policies de-identify PII.
records.gaps: Retention and deletion of prompts, outputs and agent memory are not documented.
records.options: Opt out of data sharing if required and confirm retention with ServiceNow.

records.answer: The compliance score gives the share of controls in a compliant state across mapped frameworks, and AI Risk and Compliance supports priority regulatory frameworks (Brazil).
records.gaps: Evidence collection and traceability to individual controls are not described in the pages read.
records.options: Use GRC control attestations and link agent execution records as evidence.

records.answer: Stewards approve models and MCP servers before use, and Zurich settings decide whether systems on disallowed providers keep running (Brazil and Zurich). External platform assets are inventoried with risk classification.
records.gaps: Periodic reassessment and retirement of external services are not described.
records.options: Schedule reassessments with GRC and record provider approvals on assets.

records.answer: Sessions in a self-hosted environment receive an Anthropic-signed ES256 JWT carrying the session ID, environment (pool) ID, organisation ID, runner and the creating user or service identity, verifiable against a public JWKS. Local sessions carry a session.id, account and organisation attributes on OpenTelemetry data. Neither links the agent to a release or configuration version.
records.gaps: Signed identity exists only for self-hosted cloud sessions. Local CLI sessions have no workload identity beyond the signed-in user. Any process in the session can read and present the token, and there is no revocation feed.
records.options: Use self-hosted environments where downstream services must verify the agent. Record session.id with the Claude Code version and managed settings source in your own inventory.

records.answer: The sandbox can deny or mask named credential files and environment variables. In mask mode sandboxed commands see a per-session placeholder and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value only on requests to allowed hosts. Cloud sessions keep GitHub credentials on Anthropic servers and give the VM a short-lived session-scoped credential. The Claude apps gateway holds the upstream model credential and issues...
records.gaps: Masking covers sandboxed Bash only and needs the experimental TLS termination setting. MCP servers, hooks and file tools run outside the sandbox. There is no built-in credential deny list. Rotation and revocation of tool credentials are left to the customer's secrets tooling.
records.options: Deploy sandbox.credentials mask entries through managed settings, pair with a vault-backed apiKeyHelper, and test that masked values never appear in transcripts or OTel logs.

records.answer: The self-hosted session token records an RFC 8693 act chain from the creating user or service identity through runner and environment, so downstream services can verify who started the session and issue scoped credentials. Remote MCP servers can use per-user OAuth so each developer authenticates as themselves.
records.gaps: The act chain exists only in self-hosted environments. Anthropic advises treating the token as weaker than a direct login because any code in the session can present it. Local sessions pass the developer's own credentials rather than a delegated, attenuated token.
records.options: Exchange the session token at an internal token service for short-lived, task-scoped credentials and audit by ccr:session_id and jti, as the documentation recommends.

records.answer: Agent teams and subagents exchange messages through SendMessage and local mailbox files. Claude Code tells the receiving agent the message came from another Claude session, a teammate cannot approve permission prompts or relay a denied action, and in auto mode the classifier reviews each inter-agent message before delivery.
records.gaps: Communication is between sessions of the same user on one machine through JSON files. There is no cryptographic authentication of agents or trust boundary definition, and agent teams are experimental and off by default.
records.options: Keep agent teams disabled in managed settings unless needed. For cross-boundary agent communication use an external A2A layer with its own authentication.

records.answer: Permission rules allow, ask or deny tools and specifiers such as Bash commands, Read and Edit paths and WebFetch domains, with a working directory boundary and permission modes. The OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2) restricts filesystem and network reach of shell commands. Managed settings can lock rules with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly and disable bypass or auto mode.

records.answer: User authorization (formerly on-behalf-of) passes a scoped token for the calling user to the agent, and Agent Runtime tools default to auth = user, running with the requesting user's permissions. records.answer: Orchestrator apps call subagent apps over OAuth, and the orchestrator's service principal needs CAN_USE on the target app or CAN_QUERY on a serving endpoint. Supervisor Agent only routes end users to subagents they hold grants on.

records.answer: Databricks Sandbox runs agent-written code as the requesting user by default or as the app service principal, and agent.toml tool policies can downscope sandbox table access to read only. Supervisor Agent's built-in code tool runs in a sandbox with no internet access and only the tables and volumes added.

records.answer: Unity Catalog grants decide which models, MCP services, functions, connections and data a user or service principal can call. MCP services support tool selection, and service policies can allow, deny or ask per caller, for example by tool name and OAuth client ID. User authorization scopes limit what an app can do with the user token.
records.gaps: Tool selection does not support exclusion patterns. Service policies are Beta and do not apply to Agent Services. Users with USE CONNECTION can bypass MCP tool selection.
records.options: Withhold USE CONNECTION from end users, set explicit tool lists, and test per-caller policies in Log mode before Enforce.

records.answer: Service policies on MCP services can return ASK, which pauses the tool call until a user approves it. External agents get an MCP URL-mode elicitation link and retry after approval. An identical call is not prompted again for one hour.
records.gaps: Only MCP services, input phase. Model services block on ASK. Denial, timeout and replay outside the one hour window are not described. Approver identity rules and binding beyond identical calls are not documented. Beta.

records.answer: agent.toml declares an agent's stores, tracing and tool bindings, and agentbricks deploy provisions them and grants the app service principal access, stopping before upload if a grant fails. Deployments can be listed, stopped and deleted. Service principals are created and managed by account and workspace admins and service principal managers.

records.answer: DurableAgentServer keeps run state in a Runtime Store, recovers interrupted runs after worker restarts, lets clients reconnect to stored events and deduplicates by invocation ID. Invocations in one session run in order. Supervisor Agent delegates to up to 50 subagents and tools.

records.answer: Agents are schema objects created with CREATE AGENT, owned by the creating role and listed with SHOW AGENTS. Each agent has committed immutable versions and aliases, which link the object to a release. Agents have no workload identity of their own. They run under the querying user's default role.
records.gaps: No per-agent service identity or credential. Runtime attribution is by calling user and role, not by agent principal.

records.answer: MCP connectors keep OAuth client credentials in an API integration, each user authorises the third-party service, and disabling the integration invalidates all user tokens and calls the server's revocation endpoint. Refresh token lifetime is set with OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY, which defaults to never expiring. Custom tools reach external services through SECRET objects referenced in UDF and procedure handler code...
records.gaps: Secret rotation is not documented beyond replacing or altering the secret. The pages do not state that secret values are kept out of model context. Default refresh token validity is unlimited.
records.options: Set a finite OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY, keep secrets inside handler code, and test whether tool results can echo secret material back into the agent.

records.answer: Cortex Agents determine session permissions from the querying user's default role, and each tool runs with Snowflake privileges for that caller. Cortex Analyst runs generated SQL under the calling role, CoWork applies the user's RBAC and masking policies, and MCP connectors use per-user OAuth to the third-party service. Stored procedure tools keep their owner's or caller's rights setting, and Cortex Search runs with...
records.gaps: The default role is used, not the session role. Owner's rights procedures and Cortex Search break pure user propagation, and the run API can exclude code execution under owner's rights.
records.options: Use caller's rights procedures for custom tools, set user default roles deliberately, and test with a low-privilege user.

records.answer: An agent can include an agent toolset that inherits another agent's tools at run time, and the Snowflake-managed MCP server exposes a Cortex Agent as a CORTEX_AGENT_RUN tool to external agents over OAuth. Access needs USAGE on the agent, and the MCP server enforces a maximum recursion depth of 10 invocations.
records.gaps: No A2A protocol support or agent-to-agent trust boundary model is documented. Calls run as the end user rather than as an authenticated calling agent.
records.options: Expose agents to other agents through the managed MCP server with a dedicated least-privilege role, and log calls through AI observability events.

records.answer: The code execution tool runs Python in a sandbox that can only access data passed into the session and the mounted workspace stage. It cannot query data or reach arbitrary stages, skill stages are read-only, and PyPI packages need the owner to hold PYPI_REPOSITORY_USER. The tool is enabled per agent in the spec.
records.gaps: No configurable per-agent filesystem or process policy beyond enabling the tool and package repositories. General outbound network rules for the sandbox are not described.
records.options: Leave code execution off for agents that do not need it, and test sandbox egress and file access before production.

records.answer: Every tool call is bound by Snowflake privileges: the caller needs privileges on the agent and on every object its tools use, and MCP server access does not grant tool access. Inaccessible tool handling can reject a run or drop tools the role cannot use. MCP connectors limit endpoints with API_ALLOWED_PREFIXES, custom tools reach external hosts only through external access integrations, and tool_choice can restrict...
records.gaps: Remote MCP connectors return the server's full tool list, and no per-tool allowlist inside the agent spec is documented for them.
records.options: Use the reject mode, grant per-tool privileges to dedicated roles, and expose only an agent tool on the managed MCP server.

records.answer: A response.tool_use event can carry a permission object, and a non-empty options list means the client must prompt the user before the tool runs. The client returns a permission_decision tied to that tool use, and a denial reason is passed to the model. The code execution tool defaults to permission_policy always_ask.
records.gaps: Approval is documented for code execution, not as a general per-tool policy. Replay protection and approver authorisation are not described, and the client application must implement the prompt.
records.options: Keep always_ask on, build the approval prompt in the client, and test that a decision cannot be reused for a different tool_use_id.

records.answer: Agents are created, altered and dropped with SQL, REST or Snowsight, controlled by CREATE AGENT on the schema, MODIFY to update or drop, and OWNERSHIP transfer. Creating external MCP server objects needs CREATE EXTERNAL MCP SERVER, held by account admins by default. Agent access is granted with USAGE through Snowflake roles.
records.gaps: No built-in approval step before an agent or connector goes live. ALTER replaces the full specification.
records.options: Manage agent specs through Git import and CI, and restrict MODIFY and OWNERSHIP to a release role.

records.answer: Cortex Agents run a plan, use tools, reflect loop that can split requests into subtasks and select tools per subtask. An orchestration budget caps seconds or tokens, background mode supports longer runs, and requests otherwise time out after 15 minutes.
records.gaps: Cancellation, retry and recovery of runs are not documented. The run API notes that the assistant message can occasionally fail to store.
records.options: Implement retry and cancellation in the client, or use Snowflake tasks for scheduled workflows.

records.answer: Agents and AI functions name a model or use auto, and SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS reports lifecycle status, legacy and end-of-life dates. CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION sets where inference may run, payloads are processed transiently and not persisted in the processing region, and context window limits are documented per model and region.
records.gaps: With auto, the model chosen can change. Rate limits are not documented for AI functions, and Cortex Analyst picks models from a ranked list the customer cannot set directly.
records.options: Pin models in production agents, set CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION explicitly, and restrict models with RBAC.

records.answer: The code execution tool provides a Snowflake-hosted Python 3.12 sandbox with preinstalled data libraries and optional PyPI packages. Each sandbox is scoped to one thread, reused across its requests, suspended when idle and cannot query account data. Files persist on the user's workspace stage.
records.gaps: General network egress from the sandbox is not described beyond Snowflake REST endpoints and PyPI. Isolation technology is not stated.
records.options: Test outbound network reach from the sandbox and review workspace stage contents.

records.answer: Threads hold conversation context across turns, with older turns compacted into summaries. Describe and list thread calls succeed only for the thread's owning user, and a delete endpoint removes a thread and its messages.
records.gaps: Thread retention periods are not documented. The delete endpoint does not state an ownership check.
records.options: Delete threads from the client on a schedule and confirm retention terms with Snowflake.

records.answer: Snowflake hosts the agent harness that plans, selects and executes Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, custom, MCP, web search, skills and code execution tools. It emits thinking, tool use and tool result events, checks tool access before a run and applies tool_choice.
records.gaps: The harness is managed, so its software version and change history are not visible to customers.
records.options: Pin agent versions and rerun evaluations after Snowflake releases.

records.answer: Snowflake CoWork user memory remembers preferences a user asks it to save and uses them in later conversations. Users can turn it off under Settings, which does not delete existing memories. Threads also persist until deleted.
records.gaps: Memory applies only in CoWork, not to direct agent API calls. Admin controls, retention and deletion of memories are not documented.
records.options: Confirm admin controls for memory with Snowflake and test deletion before enabling CoWork broadly.

records.answer: Model-level RBAC in SNOWFLAKE.MODELS grants per-model application roles to account roles, replacing the CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST parameter. Per-user quotas can block AI functions, Cortex Agents and CoWork when a user reaches a credit limit, resource budgets track spend per agent, and an orchestration budget caps each run. Cortex AI Guardrails screen for prompt injection and jailbreaks on Cortex Agents.
records.gaps: Quota enforcement runs within minutes, so users can overshoot. Request rate limits are not configurable in the pages read. Guardrails are account-level, need Enterprise Edition, and do not cover AI functions.
records.options: Revoke CORTEX-MODEL-ROLE-ALL from PUBLIC, set the allowlist to None, enable per-user quota blocking and enable guardrails.

records.answer: Snowflake checks privileges for each tool and checks that an MCP server and its API integration are enabled before every tool call. API_ALLOWED_PREFIXES and external access integrations limit egress, web search must be enabled by an account admin, and the prompt injection guardrail scans tool outputs. The code execution tool can require user permission.
records.gaps: No tool schema validation, per-tool rate limits or dangerous action filtering are documented. Remote MCP tool lists are not filtered per agent.
records.options: Expose a curated agent tool rather than raw SQL, and wrap risky actions in caller's rights procedures with their own checks.

records.answer: Agent and CoWork queries apply the user's RBAC, row access and masking policies. Sensitive data classification tags columns and can drive tag-based masking, AI_REDACT redacts PII in text, and a Trust Center scanner detects sensitive data accessed by agents without masking or row access policies.
records.gaps: Cortex Search runs with owner's rights, so retrieval follows the owner's view of the data. AI_REDACT is best effort and limited to US and some UK and Canadian PII.
records.options: Build search services on already masked views and enable the AI Security scanner package.

records.answer: No gateway for agent-to-agent traffic is documented. Agent toolsets and the managed MCP server rely on USAGE privileges and a recursion limit of 10, not on allowed agent pairs or schemas.
records.gaps: No allowed-pair or message schema enforcement between agents.
records.options: Control which agents can invoke others through role grants and use an external gateway for cross-platform A2A.

records.answer: End users can rate responses and leave comments, stored as CORTEX_AGENT_FEEDBACK observability events, and owners can review threads and traces in the Observability pane. Snowflake advises reviewing agent answers before showing them to users.
records.gaps: No review queue or gate that holds output for a human before release.
records.options: Build a review step in the client and sample threads from the event table.

records.answer: Agent evaluations score a version against a dataset for tool selection, tool execution, answer correctness, logical consistency and custom LLM judge metrics. Runs can be scheduled from a Task and compared side by side.
records.gaps: No anomaly detection on live behaviour is documented. Several metrics are in public preview.
records.options: Schedule evaluations after each agent or model change and alert on score drops.

records.answer: CORTEX_AI_FUNCTIONS_USAGE_HISTORY reports credits by function, model, user, role and query. CORTEX_ANALYST_USAGE_HISTORY and CORTEX_AI_GUARDRAILS_USAGE_HISTORY cover those services, and GET_SERVICE_TYPE_USAGE_V2 reports credits per agent through budgets.
records.gaps: No labour cost, savings or output measures. Requests started in CoWork are attributed to CoWork, not the agent budget.
records.options: Join usage views with business metrics in a dashboard.

records.answer: Observability metadata records latency, token usage, model name and error severity per span. Cortex Search returns HTTP 429 when overloaded and reports indexing errors after automatic suspension.
records.gaps: No load anomaly detection or capacity dashboards for Cortex services are documented.
records.options: Build alerts on span latency and error counts from the event table.

records.answer: DESCRIBE AGENT shows an agent's configured tools and resources, and inaccessible tool handling warns when a caller's role cannot use a named tool. External MCP server and API integration objects record which remote endpoints are reachable.
records.gaps: No consolidated human-readable view of each agent's reach and action scope across downstream systems. Discovered MCP tools are omitted without warning.
records.options: Query agent specs, grants and integrations to build a reach report per agent.

records.answer: Each agent turn is a trace in SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS with spans for planning, tool execution, SQL and response, recording inputs, outputs, user, role and warehouse. Rows cannot be modified, and ACCESS_HISTORY records objects and columns read and written per SQL statement.
records.gaps: Admins with AI_OBSERVABILITY_ADMIN can delete rows, trace delivery is best effort, and no retention period is stated. Access History coverage of agent tool SQL is not confirmed and needs Enterprise Edition.
records.options: Copy events to a write-once store and reconcile with QUERY_HISTORY and ACCESS_HISTORY.

records.answer: Trust Center Threat Intelligence and AI Security packages raise detections and violations, such as unusual login IPs and sensitive data accessed by agents without policies, with email and programmatic notifications. Guardrail flags are recorded in CORTEX_AI_GUARDRAILS_USAGE_HISTORY, and observability events carry user and session attributes with redaction by privilege.
records.gaps: No documented SIEM export or response ownership workflow for AI events. AI detections are few.
records.options: Forward event table and Trust Center findings to the SIEM and assign owners there.

records.answer: SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS reports each hosted model's lifecycle status and dates. The Model Registry records versions, aliases, tags and metrics for customer models with RBAC.
records.gaps: No model file scanning, AI bill of materials or compliance attestation for Cortex models is documented.
records.options: Request model provenance details from Snowflake and scan customer model artefacts before logging them.

records.answer: Hosted models are deployed within the Snowflake service perimeter, cross-region traffic is encrypted, and code execution runs in an isolated sandbox. The platform holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and IRAP among other certifications.
records.gaps: No customer-visible assurance of inference containers, harness or sandbox hosts specific to Cortex.
records.options: Review Snowflake's SOC 2 report scope for Cortex services.

records.answer: Checked the MCP connector, managed MCP server, skills and code execution pages. Snowflake does not document SBOMs, scanning or review of first-party tools, skills or custom tool code. Egress controls are covered under c3-2.
records.gaps: No tool SBOM or scanning. Skill updates apply to all agents referencing them.
records.options: Pin skills to Git commit hashes and scan UDF and procedure code in CI.

records.answer: Snowflake states that external MCP servers are not provided, maintained or verified by Snowflake, and recommends verifying third-party servers for tool poisoning and shadowing. No scanning feature is documented.
records.gaps: No scanning for squatting, tool metadata poisoning or package compromise, including PyPI packages in code execution.
records.options: Use a third-party MCP scanner and restrict CREATE EXTERNAL MCP SERVER to admins.

records.answer: Horizon sensitive data classification tags columns by semantic and privacy category and can apply tag-based masking automatically. Cortex Search requires change tracking on source tables and suspends after repeated refresh failures. AI_REDACT can sanitise text before indexing.
records.gaps: Classification needs Enterprise Edition and skips some column types. Search indexes run with owner's rights.
records.options: Classify and mask source tables before building search services and semantic views.

records.answer: Within an account, SHOW AGENTS IN ACCOUNT lists agents and CORTEX_AI_FUNCTIONS_USAGE_HISTORY shows which users call which models. External AI apps can be registered as External Agent objects for observability.
records.gaps: No discovery of AI use outside Snowflake, such as unsanctioned clients using PATs.
records.options: Review PAT and OAuth client usage in login history and use a separate shadow AI tool.

records.answer: Checked guardrails, evaluations and Trust Center pages. Evaluations measure quality and tool accuracy, not adversarial attacks, and no automated red teaming is documented.
records.gaps: No automated adversarial testing of agents, retrieval or tools.
records.options: Run an external red teaming tool against the agent API and feed results into evaluation datasets.

records.answer: Agents, Cortex Search services, semantic views, external MCP servers and External Agents are schema objects listable with SHOW commands. Cortex base models appear as objects in SNOWFLAKE.MODELS, and the Model Registry holds customer models with versions and tags.

records.options: Build an inventory from SHOW output and object tags.

records.answer: Admins can curate which agents appear in Snowflake CoWork, and only account admins can create external MCP server objects by default. Model access is granted per model through application roles.
records.gaps: No submission and approval workflow. Agents outside the curated list remain reachable by direct link.
records.options: Run approvals in a ticketing tool and restrict object creation privileges to a release role.

records.answer: Trust Center scans accounts against Security Essentials, CIS Benchmarks, Threat Intelligence and an AI Security package, recording persistent violations and one-time detections with organisation-level views of violations. AI scanners cover privileged Cortex Search owners, unrestricted Cortex Code tokens, unmasked sensitive data used by agents and a disabled prompt injection guardrail.

records.options: Enable the AI Security package and route findings to the governance dashboard.

records.answer: Checked guardrails, Trust Center and governance pages. Snowflake provides enforcement objects such as masking policies and AI_SETTINGS but no feature for writing, owning, versioning or publishing AI policies.
records.gaps: No AI policy management.
records.options: Manage AI policy in a GRC tool and map it to Snowflake enforcement settings.

records.answer: Agents move from an editable live version to immutable committed versions, with aliases such as staging and production and evaluation before deployment. Cortex base models carry legacy and end-of-life stages.
records.gaps: No use case proposal stage or gated promotion workflow.
records.options: Script promotion in CI with an evaluation score threshold.

records.answer: Every agent and MCP server object has an OWNERSHIP role, transferable with GRANT OWNERSHIP. Contacts record approver, security, steward and support contacts for tables, schemas and databases.
records.gaps: Ownership is a role, not a named person. Contacts are not listed as supported on agent objects.
records.options: Attach contacts at schema level so agents inherit them, or tag agents with an owner.

records.answer: Checked governance, Trust Center and classification pages. Snowflake classifies data sensitivity but has no use case risk assessment or risk level assignment.
records.gaps: No AI use case risk assessment.
records.options: Assess use cases in a GRC tool and use data classification as an input.

records.answer: Agent specs, including instructions, tools and models, are versioned as immutable commits with comments, and rollback repoints an alias. Versions can be imported from a stage or Git, and skills can be pinned by commit hash.
records.gaps: No approval step, and no change audit of who committed each version is described. Semantic views, permissions and search indexes are not versioned with the agent.
records.options: Gate commits and alias changes through CI with peer review.

records.answer: Checked Trust Center findings. Violations remain until fixed or resolved, but no exception record with approval, expiry or review is documented.
records.gaps: No risk acceptance workflow.
records.options: Record exceptions in a GRC tool.

records.answer: CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION controls where inference runs and customer data is not persisted in the processing region. Threads can be deleted by API, CoWork uploads are deleted after the thread TTL, and observability rows can be deleted by an admin role. Cortex Analyst does not train on customer data, and web search uses Brave with zero data retention.
records.gaps: Default retention for threads, memories and observability events is not stated. The training statement found is specific to Cortex Analyst.
records.options: Set the cross-region parameter explicitly and confirm retention and training terms contractually.

records.answer: Snowflake lists certifications such as SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27018 and IRAP Protected. Trust Center CIS Benchmark findings give account-level configuration evidence.
records.gaps: ISO 42001 is not listed. No mapping of AI controls to requirements, and Trust Center notes some benchmarks confirm only that a control exists.
records.options: Export Trust Center findings and observability evidence into a GRC tool.

records.answer: Third-party MCP connectors require admin-created objects and can be disabled, which revokes all user tokens. Web search must be enabled by an account admin, and third-party models are governed by model RBAC and lifecycle dates.
records.gaps: No periodic reassessment or third-party approval workflow.
records.options: Review connectors and model grants on a schedule in a GRC tool.

records.answer: Each agent gets an agent identity in Entra ID, created from an agent identity blueprint that holds shared description, credentials, permissions and verified publisher. A sponsor is required on every agent identity and blueprint, so each identity is linked to an accountable human. Copilot Studio creates an agent identity automatically for each new agent since May 2026, and Foundry, App Service and Teams also...
records.gaps: Linkage to runtime and release version is not part of the identity schema. Copilot Studio agents created before May 2026 still use app registrations until migrated. Foundry project agents share a project identity until published.
records.options: Record runtime and release in blueprint description, tags or custom security attributes. Migrate older Copilot Studio agents and confirm the Entra Agent ID GUID in agent metadata.

records.answer: Credentials sit on the blueprint, not on each agent identity, and managed identities used as federated identity credentials are the preferred type, with automatic rotation. Agents obtain scoped OAuth tokens per resource through multi-stage token exchange, and the Auth SDK sidecar keeps token acquisition out of application code. Disabling a blueprint or agent identity stops authentication.
records.gaps: Client secrets and certificates are still allowed. The sidecar returns bearer tokens to the agent process, so keeping them out of model context depends on the agent's design. Long-lived blueprint credentials are permitted.
records.options: Use managed identity federated credentials only and run the sidecar so the agent never holds blueprint credentials. Test that tokens are not written into prompts or tool outputs.

records.answer: Agent identities support the OAuth 2.0 on-behalf-of flow, exchanging a user token audienced to the blueprint for a resource token carrying the user's identity and delegated permissions. Conditional Access evaluates the user's policies on each OBO exchange, and refresh tokens support background work in user context. Delegated permissions are preauthorised through inheritable permissions on the blueprint.
records.gaps: Child agent identities cannot obtain interactive user consent, so admin consent on the blueprint is required. Inheritance works only within one tenant. Delegation applies only to Entra-protected resources.
records.options: Use the sidecar /Validate and /AuthorizationHeader endpoints for OBO and apply the on-behalf-of Conditional Access template.

records.answer: Agents can accept requests from other agents secured with Entra-issued tokens, and Microsoft documents four checks for inbound agent tokens including the xms_par_app_azp agent marker that names the calling blueprint. Conditional Access can block risky agents from reaching resources or other agents. Foundry supports agent identity authentication for A2A tools.
records.gaps: No A2A-specific authorisation guide was found in the Entra documentation. Cross-tenant trust boundaries for agent calls are not described beyond multitenant blueprints.
records.options: Register each callee agent as an Entra resource with app roles, require tokens audienced to it and check the caller blueprint claim.

records.answer: Agent ID governs access to Entra-protected resources through tokens. It does not control what an agent may do on its local host. Conditional Access can require a compliant device for agents' user accounts on Windows 365 Cloud PCs, which gates access rather than local actions.
records.gaps: No local action, file system or process permission model.
records.options: Use the agent runtime or endpoint controls for local scopes.

records.answer: Agent identities receive scoped access through Microsoft Graph delegated and application permissions, Azure RBAC, Entra roles, app roles, groups and access packages. Entra blocks high-privilege roles such as Global Administrator and permissions such as Application.ReadWrite.All for agents. Conditional Access controls token issuance per agent, blueprint or attribute, and Copilot Studio connector permissions appear as...
records.gaps: Applies only where the downstream system accepts Entra tokens. API keys bypass Conditional Access. Copilot Studio connector scopes are honoured only by the Power Platform connector runtime. Agent Conditional Access needs an Agent 365 licence.
records.options: Front non-Entra systems with an Entra-protected API and grant least privilege through access packages.

records.answer: Agent ID has no step that binds a human decision to a specific proposed agent action. Human approval exists for granting access, through multi-stage approvals on access package requests, which is covered under provisioning.
records.gaps: No per-action approval, denial or replay handling.
records.options: Implement action approval in the agent runtime or workflow tool.

records.answer: Agent identities are created only from blueprints through supported creation channels, with a required sponsor. Access is granted through access packages with up to three approval stages and expiry. Owners and sponsors can disable agents, disabling a blueprint blocks all its agents, and deleting a blueprint cascades a soft delete to child identities with 30-day restore.
records.gaps: Direct permission grants outside access packages have no expiry or review. Cascade cleanup can lag by hours or days. Governance features need an Agent 365 licence with Entra P1 or E3, or Microsoft 365 E7.
records.options: Route all agent access through access packages and monitor audit logs for direct grants.

records.answer: Agent ID is an identity service and does not sequence, retry or recover agent workflows.
records.gaps: Outside product category.
records.options: Use Copilot Studio, Foundry or another orchestration layer.

records.answer: Agent ID does not run models or manage model versions and endpoints.
records.gaps: Outside product category.
records.options: Use the inference platform's controls.

records.answer: Agent ID does not host the harness or code interpreter. The Auth SDK sidecar is a container the customer deploys beside the agent, not an execution environment.
records.gaps: Outside product category.
records.options: Use the hosting platform's sandbox controls.

records.answer: Agent ID does not store session state for agents.
records.gaps: Outside product category.
records.options: Use the agent platform's session store.

records.answer: Agent ID does not provide a harness that executes tools.
records.gaps: Outside product category.

records.answer: Agent ID does not store chat or long-term memory.
records.gaps: Outside product category.
